steps: pnpm --filter property-explorer test :: success :: 31s — real vitest output with named suites
Records copy guard (P-85 item 16) :: success :: 0s :: log 'Records copy guard passed (240 files scanned).'
Retired checkout seam guard (P-103) :: success :: 0s :: log 'P-103 seam-retired guard passed (4 checks, each with a live positive control).'
Public pages guard (P-108) :: success :: 0s :: log 'P-108 public-pages guard passed (6 checks over 3 static pages, each with a live positive control).'
falsifier4_theTestJobReallyExecutes.theCorrection: My pre-registered discriminator was 'executed = conclusion success AND duration > 0s'. It reported the three guard steps as NOT EXECUTED. The raw timestamps show all three ran inside 2026-09-17T19:21:23Z — GitHub's step timestamps have one-second granularity, so start and end land on the same second. The discriminator that can separate execution from a no-op is the step's own log output, and it is present for all three. Refined rule: executed = conclusion success AND (non-zero duration OR its own log output present); `skipped` is never execution. Had the log been absent, 'success, no output, 0s' would have been a defect finding about the JOB, and it would have been reported as one.

falsifier5_added_duplicateNamesAreSafe.reading: Two check-runs with the same required name on one head did not confuse the evaluation. Blast radius on command-center-ci.yml and factory-console-ci.yml changes is safe. The cost: such a change now also runs the full Property Explorer suite.
falsifier5_added_duplicateNamesAreSafe.observationOnTheSameRun: Command Center CI's `test` job carries a step `Live GREEN smoke (WDLL 8)` that is `skipped` on every pull request by construction (`if: workflow_dispatch && inputs.live_smoke`) while the job's own verdict is `success`. That is the 91_branch_protection_runbook 'a required check is satisfied by skipped' hazard, live, in a producer of the required context. Not a defect in this fix, not fixed here, routed in the close.

whatChangedInMyUnderstanding.before: I treated `test` as Property Explorer CI's check (the dispatch's premise, and CP1 recorded that the premise was true but incomplete).
whatChangedInMyUnderstanding.after: Control D showed the incompleteness in the direction that matters for the fix's blast radius: a command-center-ci.yml-only diff already produced its OWN `test` before this change, so the fix adds a SECOND producer on those heads rather than creating the first. The required context has never guaranteed 'the PE suite ran'; it guarantees 'some workflow's job named test succeeded'. That is why a context-set review is in the close rather than a comment.
whatChangedInMyUnderstanding.whyItMatters: It bounds the claim I am entitled to make: this fix makes the context REACHABLE from every workflow-file change. It does not make `test` mean the same suite every time, and the close must not let the operator read it as if it did.

whatChangedInMyUnderstanding.before: The pre-registered coverage claim was 'workflow files are the class that can change without producing test'.
whatChangedInMyUnderstanding.after: Measured, not asserted: on main today, 19 of 770 tracked files can change without producing `test` across 14 classes; after this fix, 16 across 12. The three the fix brings under a required trigger are exactly the three workflow files that are not self-referenced (property-explorer-sync-retrieval-key.yml, publish-map-renderer.yml, source-encoding.yml). The remaining 16 files include one that genuinely surprises: `packages/instrument-registry/**` ships a `src/index.test.ts` that NO workflow runs, so a test suite exists whose inputs are in no required trigger.
whatChangedInMyUnderstanding.method: The path lists were PARSED OUT OF THE WORKFLOW FILES at each ref (git show <ref>:<file>) rather than hardcoded, and the parser reproduces the earlier hand-checked measurement (770/751/19) on main, which is the validation that it is measuring the right thing.

whatChangedInMyUnderstanding.before: CP1 listed the stale workaround comment in command-center-ci.yml as a contradiction I had measured (PR #411 reported `test` on a PE-only diff, so the comment's stated consequence did not occur).
whatChangedInMyUnderstanding.after: Still unedited and still live, but the mechanism is now fully explained rather than just contradicted: the comment prescribes including command-center-ci.yml in a PE pull request's diff to make the context report. The PE-only baseline shows that workaround was never necessary — and after #412 lands, a command-center-ci.yml change ALSO triggers Property Explorer CI, which is the same workaround arriving structurally. The comment becomes more wrong with this fix, not less. It is routed, not patched, because it is outside the smallest form and correcting prose is not the defect fix.

theAdversarialMoveThisCheckpointRan.question: What would have to be true for the whole fix to be worthless?
theAdversarialMoveThisCheckpointRan.answer: That the required context were bound to a workflow identity rather than to the bare check-run name. The protection object carries no workflow qualifier (app_id 15368, context `test`), which is evidence, not proof, that the name is the key.
theAdversarialMoveThisCheckpointRan.howTheRunSettledIt: Under the identity hypothesis, #412's head would still have been refused. It reported `test :: completed :: success` and came back CLEAN. The premise the fix rests on is now measured in the direction that matters instead of assumed.
theAdversarialMoveThisCheckpointRan.residual: The mixed duplicate case (two producers of `test` on one head, one success and one failure) is NOT measured. It is a question about the required-context design, not about this fix, and it is in the close's open questions rather than guessed at.
